subject: Re: NexonHealth performance & stability questionnaire
summary: NexonHealth asked for detailed performance and stability metrics for their RFP. The thread includes an initial questionnaire request, our delivered questionnaire attachment, a sample workload from the customer, and an internal plan outlining test windows, hardware, and deliverables.
messages:
From: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@nexonhealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T23:12:00Z
Subject: Request: Performance & Stability Questionnaire — NexonHealth RFP

Hi Dev / Rishi,

Thanks for the overview call earlier. As part of NexonHealth's procurement packet we need a detailed performance questionnaire and concrete benchmarking figures that we can include in our evaluation. Specifically we are asking for:

- P50/P95/P99 latency for single- and multi-turn chat generation at 32/256/1024 token lengths.
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) at QPS levels of 50, 500, and 1,000 with representative payloads.
- Tail-behavior under burst traffic: 10s and 60s spikes to 2x/5x baseline QPS.
- Failure/fallback behavior when compute is constrained (e.g., model fallback, queued requests) and expected degradation modes.
- Test methodology: data sanitization, warmup, seed inputs, seeding for KV cache, and exact model/config used.

We would like both aggregated metrics and raw logs/Prometheus metrics for independent verification. Attached is the RFP section that lists acceptable formats and a simple sample workload we hope to use (we can refine).

Can you confirm whether you can provide P99's for the above scenarios and a proposed 2-week window you can run tests? Also note our compliance/security team requires that any logs shared are scrubbed of PHI.

Thanks,
Sara Lambert
Head of Cloud Procurement — NexonHealth

Attachments: nexon_rfp_section_5.pdf (pdf), sample-workload-template.csv (csv)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@nexonhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T01:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Performance & Stability Questionnaire — NexonHealth RFP

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the sample workload. We can run the benchmarks and deliver both aggregated metrics and the raw Prometheus/JSON traces with PHI redaction.

Attached is our performance questionnaire template (redwood_perf_questionnaire_v2.xlsx) — we populated the first 2 sections with example outputs from a recent internal run to show the format. A few clarifying notes up front:

- Test hardware: we run the public-facing benchmarks on A100 80GB and Ampere-based V100-equivalent pools; for private deployments we will replicate on your target GPU type if provided.
- Model variants: results depend on model size + quantization. Please indicate which model family/version you plan to evaluate; otherwise we will run on the open model listed in the RFP (gptx-13b-quantized and reference fp16).
- Caching and batching: our serving runtime uses automatic prefix KV caching and adaptive batching. For reproducibility we will run 3 modes: cold-start (no cache), steady-state (warm cache + dynamic batching), and stress (saturated batching).
- Test windows: propose 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-17 for a staged run (staging -> canary -> scale test). We can shorten if you need faster turnaround.

Deliverables: populated questionnaire (xlsx), a CSV of the raw request/response latencies, Prometheus metrics export, and a short report describing anomalies and fallback events.

Please confirm workload CSV and whether you consent to sharing anonymized request payload hashes for root-cause later. Once confirmed we'll lock test configs and schedule the runs.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_perf_questionnaire_v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nexonhealth.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@nexonhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Performance & Stability Questionnaire — NexonHealth RFP

Dev — thanks for the fast turnaround and the template. We attached the workload we expect to use in testing (nexon_workload_profile.csv). A couple of clarifications from our side before you schedule:

1) Payload composition: ~65% short prompts (~40 tokens), 25% medium (~200 tokens), 10% long (~900–1,200 tokens). We will provide exact tokenized lengths in the attached CSV.
2) Concurrency profile: baseline 200 QPS, expected peak 1,200 QPS for up to 2 minutes, and sustained 800 QPS for 15 minutes during monthly reporting.
3) Acceptance criteria: P95 latency < 250ms for short prompts, P99 < 400ms for short prompts, and graceful degradation (queueing or fallback) rather than crashes.
4) Security note: all provided samples have no PHI. We will mark any subset that might be sensitive.

Can you confirm which exact metrics you will provide (we need P50/P95/P99, per-model+per-token breakdown, and a per-run config file). Also please confirm whether the staging runs will use customer-specified GPU types (we can provide access to our test instance types if needed).

Thanks — Tom
Senior Systems Architect, NexonHealth

Attachments: nexon_workload_profile.csv (csv)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nexonhealth.com>, Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@nexonhealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Performance & Stability Questionnaire — NexonHealth RFP

Tom / Sara — appreciate the workload and acceptance criteria. Quick response with the proposed test plan and what we'll deliver: 

Planned test windows (US-PST timezone):
- 2026-11-12: staging validation (low-impact, smoke tests, confirm configs)
- 2026-11-14: canary runs at 200/500 QPS for baseline metrics
- 2026-11-16: scale stress test (targeting 1,200 QPS spike windows)

Hardware & runtime:
- Default: A100-80GB (CUDA 12, cuDNN optimized kernels)
- Alternate (by request): A30 / T4 parity runs for cost-performance comparables
- Serving runtime: Redwood inference engine v1.9.3 with KV cache enabled in the steady-state runs
- Model configs captured in test-config-20261112.yaml — we will include tokenizer versions and quantization parameters.

Metrics and artifacts we will provide after each run (zipped):
- Aggregated CSV with P50/P95/P99, mean, std, requests/sec, tokens/sec per bucket (short/medium/long).
- Prometheus scrape (raw) + Grafana snapshot links.
- Server-side traces showing queue length and batching behavior.
- A short incident log enumerating any fallback events or throttling decisions.

Security & PHI: all logs we share will be sanitized. We will replace request bodies with sha256 hashes and provide a separate mapping file only if you sign an NDA addendum (per your security ask).

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the windows above or propose alternate 48-hour windows. Once we have confirmation we will provision the test harness and share the CloudWatch/Prometheus endpoints for live monitoring.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
